prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Kansas City. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Kansas City Missouri for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — I just need one quick detail: do you mean Kansas City, Missouri or Kansas City, Kansas (or a ZIP code)? That lets me find practices closest to you and check who is currently taking patients.

Meanwhile, here’s how to decide which specific offices to call and why — plus what to ask when you call. If you want, I’ll use your ZIP/city and return a short, prioritized list (name, address, phone, why I picked them).

Which practices to call (and why)
- Board‑certified oral & maxillofacial surgeons
  - Why: They do the surgical placement of implants and manage complex medical issues, bone grafts, sinus lifts, and IV sedation/GA when needed. Call one for surgical evaluation and if you’ve been told you need grafting or have medical risks.
- Board‑certified periodontists (gum specialists)
  - Why: Periodontists place implants and specialize in soft-tissue and bone health around implants. Good choice if you have periodontal disease or need aesthetic gum work.
- Prosthodontists (implant restorations and full-mouth rehabilitation)
  - Why: They specialize in designing and restoring implant crowns, bridges, and full-arch solutions (All‑on‑4, hybrid prostheses). Call one if you want complex restorative planning or a long-term prosthesis.
- Implant-focused general dentists
  - Why: Many general dentists place implants and handle routine single-tooth cases. They can be more convenient/cheaper for straightforward cases.
- Dental school clinic (UMKC School of Dentistry)
  - Why: University clinics often provide high-quality care at lower cost; treatment is supervised by specialists-in-training and faculty. Good option if cost is a concern.

What to ask when you call (so you can compare)
- Do you have a specialist on staff for implant placement (oral surgeon, periodontist, prosthodontist)? Which one will treat me?
- Do you do CBCT (3D) imaging at your office?
- Do you offer bone grafting, sinus lifts, and sedation (oral/IV)?
- How many implants does the provider place per year? Are they board certified?
- Do you handle the restoration (crown/bridge) in-house or refer it out?
- Typical timeline from consult to finished crown, and estimated cost ranges for a single implant (implant + abutment + crown).
- Do you accept my insurance / offer financing or implant warranties/guarantees?
- Are you currently accepting new patients, and what is the wait time?

If you give me your ZIP code or street side (KC, MO vs KS) and any preferences (insurance, sedation, cost), I’ll compile 4–6 specific, highly rated practices near you with phone numbers, addresses, specialties, and why I recommend each.
